# Interway

> Interway is a free route planner for boats on European inland waterways and coastal seas ("Google Maps for
> boats"). It finds routes through rivers, canals, lakes and locks, joins them to a sea route network
> (Baltic, North Sea, Channel, Atlantic coast, Mediterranean, Black Sea), and lists what a route passes: locks
> (with chamber sizes), bridges (with clearance), marinas, ports, fuel, water, pump-outs and towns.
> Routing runs in the browser from OpenStreetMap data. Not for navigation.

## How an AI assistant can use it

The page URL fully describes a route. Write a link, give it to the user, and they open it:

    https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=LON,LAT&to=LON,LAT

Parameters (decimal degrees, longitude first):

- `from`, `to`: start and destination, `lon,lat`
- `via`: waypoints in order, `lon,lat;lon,lat` (use these to force a particular way, e.g. through a canal)
- `draft`, `air` (air draft), `beam`, `len`: vessel dimensions in metres; routes avoid waterways too small
  (defaults: draft 1 m, air draft 3 m, beam 0.5 m, length 9 m: pass the real boat's values)
- `speed`: cruising speed, km/h (default 10); `current`: river current assumed where no researched value exists,
  m/s (default 0.5); `lockmin`: minutes per lock (default 20)
- `avoidLocks=1`: prefer routes with fewer locks
- `avoidSea=1`: keep to inland waterways wherever an inland way exists (open sea already counts 1.5x by default)
- `date=YYYY-MM-DD`: departure date. Daily stages get dates, each waterway is checked for the month the boat
  reaches it (usually closed, low water, high water, ice), and waterways usually closed then are avoided where
  another way exists, but never by adding more than about 100 km of open sea: then the inland way is kept and
  warned about. Water levels change by month: a route possible in May may not be in August; the brief says in
  which months all the route's waterways are usually open.
- `coastal=1`: for a small boat, keep near the coast (within about 10 km of land), harbour to harbour, instead
  of crossing open sea (e.g. round the Gulf of Lion rather than straight across)

Other links:

- `?place=LON,LAT`: opens the card of the harbour, lock or town there (within 200 m), with its facts (VHF,
  phone, services), or a pin: link a stop for the user.
- `?waterway=ID`: opens a researched waterway sheet (IDs are in the brief's `waterways[].id`; the Markdown brief
  lists each sheet's link).
- Permalinks ("Copy permalink" under a route) spell out every setting and add `data=VERSION&was=KM,LOCKS`: the
  data version the route was planned on and its distance and locks then. Opened later on newer data, the page
  says what changed. The brief's JSON has the data version in `data`.
- Snapshots ("Save snapshot") are a JSON file with the exact route and brief; "Open snapshot" shows them as saved,
  not recomputed, until the user asks to recompute on today's data.

The link is the whole route: settings saved in the user's browser do not change a route opened from a link with
`from` and `to`, and the values you give stay in the link (the brief marks only dimensions you left out as
"default, not entered"). The route shown is the fastest one (time underway, with open sea counted 1.5x); the
page also offers alternatives. Daily stages are up to 8 h underway; a non-stop sea passage is one stage.

Examples:

- Wrocław to Amsterdam: https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=17.035,51.115&to=4.90,52.38
- Warsaw to Gdańsk on the Vistula, 1.2 m draft: https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=21.03,52.25&to=18.66,54.35&draft=1.2
- London to Crete by sea: https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=-0.075,51.507&to=25.14,35.345

## Using Interway from ChatGPT, Claude or another assistant

A prompt a user can paste (replace the places, dates and boat):

    Plan a boat trip from Wrocław to Monaco with https://abecadel.github.io/interway/ (read
    https://abecadel.github.io/interway/llms.txt first). Boat: motor cruiser, length 9 m, beam 3 m, draft 1.2 m,
    air draft 3 m, 10 km/h. Departure 2027-05-01. Build the route link with every parameter, open it, read the
    route brief (or call the site tools if your browser has them), and give me: the route and why, daily stages,
    locks, the lowest bridge and shallowest stretch against my boat, the waterways closed or risky in the months I
    reach them, and the notices I must check before I go.

Without a browser the assistant can still write the link (see above) for the user to open, and the user can
paste back the brief ("Copy brief for AI"). Waterway facts in the brief carry the date they were checked and
their sources: closures change, so tell the user to confirm them with the authority named there.

## Route brief

After a route is computed the user can press "Copy brief for AI" and paste a Markdown brief into the chat:
distance and time, locks, open-sea distance, towns, the countries crossed (from which km), fuel, water and
harbours with the longest stretch without each, a "Before you go" checklist (licences, permits, vignettes, taxes,
entry formalities, notices to read, data still to give), the tightest mapped draft, headroom, beam and length
limits on the route and whether the boat fits, legs, daily stages (with dates, and the VHF channel, phone and
services of the harbour each day ends at), every stop with its kilometre, hazards, researched waterway sheets,
boating rules by country, and the route link with these parameters. "JSON" downloads the same brief as
structured data (fields `checklist`, `limits`, `countries`, `services`, `stages`, `waterways`, `rules`, ...).

## Site tools (WebMCP)

In browsers with WebMCP (`document.modelContext`, e.g. the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in browser) the page
registers tools an agent can call directly:

- `plan_route({from, to, via?, vessel?})`: `from`/`to`/`via` are place names ("Port Hercule, Monaco") or
  `{lon, lat}`; `vessel` takes `draft`, `airDraft`, `beam`, `length`, `speedKmh`, `currentMs`, `lockPenaltyMin`,
  `avoidLocks`, `avoidSea`, `coastal`, `departure` (YYYY-MM-DD). Returns the brief (as JSON).
- `get_route_brief()`, `list_stops({types?})`: the route on the page; after `set_vessel` or a waypoint change
  they wait while the route is recomputed (up to a minute).
- `set_vessel({...})` (same fields as `vessel`), `add_waypoint({point, index?})`, `remove_waypoint({index})`,
  `find_place({query})`.

Place names go to an online geocoder first and fall back to the waterway places in the data (locks, marinas,
towns); give coordinates when a name is ambiguous.

## Coverage and limits

- Inland: Poland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, France, the United Kingdom (Thames, Broads, the Canal & River Trust and Scottish canals), Austria, Czechia, Slovakia, the Danube to the Black Sea (Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria), northern Italy (the Po, its idrovie and the Litoranea Veneta; lakes Garda, Maggiore, Como), Ireland and Northern Ireland (Shannon, Shannon–Erne Waterway, Erne, Grand and Royal canals, Barrow) Sweden (Göta kanal, Trollhätte kanal, Vänern, Vättern, Mälaren and the canals off them), Finland (the Saimaa lake system and its canals), Lithuania (Nemunas from Kaunas, Neris, Curonian Lagoon), the Vistula and Szczecin lagoons, Spain (Guadalquivir to Seville, Ría de Bilbao, lower Guadiana), Portugal (Douro to Pocinho with its locks, Tejo, Sado, Guadiana), Denmark (Limfjord), Norway (Telemark Canal, Skien → Dalen, and down to the sea at Langesund through Porsgrunn), Estonia (Emajõgi, Lake Peipus), Latvia (Daugava, Lielupe), and the Danube from Kelheim to all three delta arms (Kilia, Sulina, Sfântu Gheorghe). English narrow canals take boats up to 2.08 m (7 ft) beam.
- When no route fits the vessel, the error names each structure that blocks it and its limit (e.g. "Staircase Top Lock
  Gate (km 20) limits beam to 2.08 m, yours is 3 m"); if the points are not connected at all, it says so.
- Navigation mode ("Start navigation" under a route, in the browser with GPS): the map follows the boat heading up and shows the next lock or bridge, speed and course over ground, cross-track error and ETA; it re-plans from the boat's position when it leaves the route, warns before locks and bridges (vibration, optional voice) and records a GPX track. "Save map for offline" stores the map along a route. These have no URL parameters.
- Sea: European seas from the Atlantic coast to the Black Sea, including the whole Mediterranean with harbours and marinas of every coastal country (Greece and the Corinth Canal, Turkey, Malta, Cyprus, the Adriatic, North Africa), as a coarse coastal network.
- Sea depth: open-sea legs carry the charted depth from EMODnet bathymetry (about 0.5 km grid, minus a 0.5 m
  margin). Routes go round stretches too shallow for the given `draft` where a deeper way exists; where none
  does (the coarse network crosses banks that real boats pass in dredged channels, e.g. estuaries) the route
  still goes through, and the brief gives the shallowest stretch and the km charted shallower than the draft.
  The first ~1.5 km off the shore, harbour approaches and inland waterways have no depth data.
- Researched waterway sheets (navigability, depth, bridges, current, locks and hours, typical conditions by month,
  tides, closures, the authority and its notices, with sources and the date checked) cover the waterways of the
  Wrocław → Monaco routes so far; the brief's "Waterways" section lists those on a route. Elsewhere, and for
  today's water levels and notices, check with the waterway authority.
- Waters where OpenStreetMap says motorboats are not allowed are avoided where another way exists (the brief says
  how far a route still crosses them), and posted speed limits slow the boat in the time estimate.
- Rules by country: the brief's "Rules by country" section gives, for each country the route passes, what a
  visiting pleasure boat needs: licence and its thresholds, whether foreign licences or the ICC count, permits,
  vignettes and tolls, registration, radio, speed limits, alcohol limit, equipment, waters closed to motorboats,
  and at sea the coastal speed zones, anchoring bans, entry and customs and taxes, with sources and the date
  checked. Waterway sheets add each waterway's own rules (motorboats allowed or not, speed limit, permit).
- Bridges and lock chambers are listed with their limits only where OpenStreetMap records them; many do not.
  The waterway sheets give each waterway's usual draft and lowest bridge, and routes go round waterways whose
  sheet limits the boat exceeds (or warn where there is no other way).

Data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), towns © GeoNames (CC BY 4.0), bathymetry © EMODnet (CC BY 4.0). Source: https://github.com/abecadel/interway
